title: Parker's drug use and practice habits
summary: Parker told him he began hard drugs at fourteen, out-practiced everyone, and visited Buster Smith in Dallas.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But before that, we had talked about how he became involved in the drug situation. He explained to me it happened to him when he was about 14 years old. And he also told me how his mother had the policeman to break the door down in Kansas City to get him and Tadd Dameron out of the room; they had been in the room for four months practicing. They'd take everything they needed in that room, and just lock up. See, that's the way he did it. He out-practiced everybody. Besides being treasured with that genius, he still out-practiced everybody. You see, he practiced long periods, like round the clock, and then he wouldn't practice any more, you know. But he could go and make this great bi change in himself, you know, during these long practice
periods. And he'd just disappear off the scene. After so long, you wouldn't see Charlie Parker -- he was gone.

He told me later on that sometimes he would go to Dallas, Texas, and spend time with Buster Smith, the saxophone player that wrote "One O'Clock Jump" with Basie, that used to play the lead alto with Basie. That was one of his early tutors, and he loved Buster, and he would go and spend time with Buster Smith, you know, in Dallas, Texas.
Did he say exactly how he got involved in ...(?)...?

Yeah. I would hate to say that on this tape. But it was somebody who was close to him who turned him on to drugs when he was fourteen years old -- hard drugs. And then he told me about this book that his mother left him in his room one time about inhibitions, you know. And he said she never really got on his case, you know; she would just do these different things. She loved him. She was a nurse. She loved him, and she was just trying to guide him the best she could without really being harsh toward him, you know.
